html:
The Ngarinyin are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Kimberley in Western Australia, in the plateau country of the upper Isdell and Durack rivers. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Speaking of their lands, they call themselves the Wilinggin people. Their language is also known as Ungarinyin.

With the Worrorra and Wunambal they share the law of the Wandjina, rain and creator beings painted in rock shelters across the region, and their country holds many of the older Gwion Gwion figures. Other neighbours were the Wurla to the south and the Kwini to the northeast.

Cattle stations reached parts of their land in the early 1900s. In 1956 many Ngarinyin moved with the Worrorra to Mowanjum near Derby. The elder David Mowaljarlai worked for years to explain Ngarinyin law to outsiders, and in 2004 their native title was recognised over Wilinggin country.
